evals.prompt: I'm on branch feat/config-discover and I'm ready to open a PR. Can you create it for me?
evals.expected_output: A PR title in conventional commits format and a description following the repo's .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md (## Problem, ## Solution, ## How to Test). The PR targets develop.
assertions: PR title follows conventional commits format: type(scope): description
PR description contains ## Problem, ## Solution, and ## How to Test sections
The Solution section explains *why* decisions were made, not just *what* was changed
The base branch is develop (not main, and not dynamically re-detected)
The description follows the repo's .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md structure, and the skill does not look for a commitlint.config.js (pier uses .commitlint.yaml)

evals.prompt: I replaced the client-go approach with shelling out to kubectl for the exec model. Create a PR for feat/kubectl-shellout.
evals.expected_output: A PR with a conventional commits title and a description using the default template. The Solution section should explain why shelling out to kubectl was chosen over client-go, and note the trade-off (inherits the user's kubeconfig/EKS exec auth for free).
assertions: PR title follows conventional commits format: type(scope): description
PR description contains a ## Solution section that explains why shelling out to kubectl was chosen over client-go
Solution section mentions the trade-off or reasoning (e.g. inheriting existing kubeconfig/EKS auth)
